what: ci-wait migration misses its own edit-in-sync surfaces
scenario_or_breakage: The plan updates ci-wait.md wording but leaves rebase-rebump prose and related test/docs pinned to synchronous-only, so post-PR guidance conflicts and structural checks can preserve the old contract
suggested_fix: Update every ci-wait synchronous-only site listed in ci-wait.md, including rebase-rebump-subprocedure and ci-wait exit-trap docs/tests, or explicitly keep ci-wait outside the new paired-PID Family B contract

what: Timeout signaling only targets the top-level PID
scenario_or_breakage: Family B scripts often block in child commands such as sleep, gh, or external launchers; killing only the shell PID can still leave the actual long-running child orphaned after monitor timeout
suggested_fix: Use a supervisor/process-group or per-script TERM trap strategy that terminates tracked child PIDs, and add a test where the paired PID is a shell currently waiting on a child process

what: New PID-file lint checks are fence-global rather than launch-specific
scenario_or_breakage: A single LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE token and one --paired-pid-file monitor invocation can satisfy every Family B anchor in a multi-launch fence, leaving another launch effectively unpaired while lint passes
suggested_fix: Make the linter associate allocation/export and monitor argv with each denylisted anchor, or reject multiple Family B anchors per fence unless each has its own paired PID-file block; add a negative multi-anchor fixture

what: Proposed PID writer validates less than the monitor/docs require
scenario_or_breakage: The helper plan only checks absolute/no-dotdot before writing, while the monitor/docs require session tmpdir scope and symlink rejection; an ambient LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE can make scripts write a PID file outside the intended session surface
suggested_fix: Share or mirror the monitor path validation for LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE before writing, including session tmpdir containment, symlink rejection, and regular-file/parent checks, while still failing open for callers
